title: The vZEN API: Virtual Service Edge clusters and nodes

endpoints.statement: The Go SDK manages Virtual Service Edge clusters at /zia/api/v1/virtualZenClusters and Virtual Service Edge nodes at /zia/api/v1/virtualZenNodes.

vzen-is-vse.statement: The SDK's vZEN types are the Virtual Service Edge: the cluster type documents itself as the Virtual Service Edge cluster, and the node type as the Virtual Service Edge.

quotes: // Name of the Virtual Service Edge cluster

cluster-model.statement: The cluster model carries a status (ENABLED, DISABLED, DISABLED_BY_SERVICE_PROVIDER or NOT_PROVISIONED_IN_SERVICE_PROVIDER), the cluster IP, subnet mask and default gateway, an ipSecEnabled flag, and a virtualZenNodes member list that the SDK documents as needing at least two instances.

quotes: // Supported Values: ENABLED, DISABLED, DISABLED_BY_SERVICE_PROVIDER, NOT_PROVISIONED_IN_SERVICE_PROVIDER
// A Virtual Service Edge cluster must contain at least two Virtual Service Edge instances.
// A Boolean value that specifies whether to terminate IPSec traffic from the client at selected Virtual Service Edge instances for the Virtual Service Edge cluster

node-model.statement: The node model carries a deploymentMode of STANDALONE or CLUSTER (CLUSTER only on VMware ESXi), a loadBalancerIpAddress that applies only when the deployment mode is CLUSTER, an inProduction flag, a status that can also be IN_TRIAL, and a vzenSkuType of SMALL, MEDIUM or LARGE.

quotes: // Specifies the deployment mode. Select either STANDALONE or CLUSTER if you have the VMware ESXi platform. Otherwise, select only STANDALONE.
// The IP address of the load balancer. This field is applicable only when the 'deploymentMode' field is set to CLUSTER.
// Represents the Virtual Service Edge instances deployed for production purposes

tf-lb-ip-doc-example-standalone.summary: Whether `load_balancer_ip_address` is meaningful on a STANDALONE Virtual Service Edge node in Terraform.

quotes: This field is applicable only when the 'deploymentMode' field is set to `CLUSTER`.

positions.says: The argument documentation says the load balancer IP applies only when the deployment mode is CLUSTER.
The first example sets load_balancer_ip_address together with deployment_mode STANDALONE.

tf-lb-ip-doc-example-standalone.impact: The provider schema marks the attribute optional and the example sets it for a standalone node, so the provider does not reject the combination. Do not read a set load balancer IP on a standalone node as proof the platform uses it.
